haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same events and writes its invoices to the shadow store only.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store and never charges.
haiku-low.q3: Gate 1 needs 7 consecutive days with mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person makes the move by setting the flag.
haiku-low.q4: Charge failure rate above 2% in any 10-minute window, in both or new_only, starts an automatic rollback and pages on-call. Ignored if a rollback is already running.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only, after RB5 confirms one ledger charge per due period. Then the flag flips, the record closes, and gates reset. Re-entry is by person-set steps from old_only.
haiku-low.q6: It stops at day 35 in new_only, when the timer locks it with no rollback edge. The doc gives no further reason beyond events leaving the log.
haiku-low.q7: Workers read billing_mode from the config service. If it is unreadable they keep their last known mode. NOT STATED for an invoice in process at the switch.
haiku-low.q8: Gate and sign-off decisions are recorded with who and when, in the config service. Gate counts come from the shadow store. A person must make each forward move; a met gate only allows it.
haiku-low.q9: NOT STATED which component detects it. It measures charge failure rate above 2% in any 10-minute window. It starts rollback at RB1 and pages on-call.
haiku-low.q10: RB1 fences the new engine so it starts no new charges, and charges are delayed, not lost. The old engine charges due periods at RB4, after reconcile and reprocess.
haiku-low.q11: Both engines send the idempotency key (customer, billing_period) to the payment provider, and the ledger enforces uniqueness on that key. RB4 skips periods already in the ledger.
haiku-low.q12: Billing stays fenced in rb_blocked, the flag does not flip, and on-call is paged. On-call fixes the cause and retries from RB2, which is safe because charges are idempotent.

sonnet.q1: The old engine computes, charges and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same events and writes only to the shadow store.
sonnet.q2: The new engine computes, charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store and never charges.
sonnet.q3: Gate 1 must be met: 7 consecutive days with a mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person makes the move by setting the flag.
sonnet.q4: A charge failure rate above 2% in any 10-minute window starts rollback automatically at RB1 and pages on-call. This applies in both and new_only. It is ignored if a rollback is already running.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. To take over again, the rollout must re-enter shadow from old_only, which resets the gates so the 7-day count starts at zero. Gate 1 must then be met again, and a person makes each forward move.
sonnet.q6: It stops at day 35 in new_only, when a timer moves the mode to new_only_locked, provided no rollback record is open. The document says that is the one-way lock, and it says that day's first events leave the 35-day event log at that point.
sonnet.q7: Workers read billing_mode from the config service. NOT STATED: how they are notified of a change, such as polling or push. NOT STATED: what happens to an invoice being processed at that moment. The document says only that idempotency keys prevent double charges if workers disagree.
sonnet.q8: Gate evidence is computed from the shadow store (comparison results), not stored as a count. Gate and sign-off decisions are recorded with who and when. Nothing technically blocks promotion: a met gate allows a move but a person still makes it. NOT STATED: any enforcement mechanism beyond that.
sonnet.q9: NOT STATED which component detects it. The condition is the new engine's charge failure rate above 2% in any 10-minute window, in both or new_only. When it is met, automatic rollback starts at RB1 and on-call is paged.
sonnet.q10: The new engine starts no new charges once the fence is on. In-flight calls finish. The charges are delayed, not lost. The old engine makes them at RB4, charging each due period that has no ledger charge, using the idempotency key.
sonnet.q11: The idempotency key (customer, billing_period) is sent to the payment provider, and the ledger enforces uniqueness on the same key. In RB4, periods already in the ledger are skipped whichever engine charged them. RB2 reconciles unknown outcomes against the ledger and provider, and RB5 verifies exactly one charge per due period.
sonnet.q12: It goes to rb_blocked. The fence stays on, so the new engine does not charge. The flag does not flip, and on-call is paged. On-call fixes the cause and retries from RB2. Re-running is safe because charges are idempotent. There is no automatic exit. Whether the old engine charges while the rollback is blocked is NOT STATED.
